## Visit times

The input is the imported REDCap table; the output still has one row per participant and recorded visit. `mutate()` creates or changes columns without summarizing the rows. `case_when()` maps each event name to its scheduled month, stored in `time_linear`.

#| label: visit-times

## Baseline values

Study arm, child or adult, preferred language and the consent and follow-up dates are recorded only on each participant's baseline row (`baseline_variables`, on [Setup](setup.qmd)). This step takes them from the baseline rows, one row per participant, so that the next step can copy them to every visit. Because they come from the baseline row itself, the order of rows in the export does not matter. A participant with two baseline rows stops the run, since there would be no way to tell which is right; a participant with visits but no baseline row keeps missing values, with a warning.

```{r}
#| label: baseline-values
#| eval: false
```

## Build visit data

`time_factor` stores the visit as a category for the models, with its levels in time order, baseline first, whatever order the rows arrive in. The baseline values are then joined to every visit by participant: a visit keeps its own value if it has one and otherwise takes the baseline value. The join is declared "many-to-one" (many visits, one baseline row per participant), so a repeated participant stops the run rather than multiplying visits. This carries assignment and baseline subgroup information, not a missed visit's outcome score.

Selected 999 codes become `NA`, R's missing-value marker. The separate language recode currently assigns 999 to English; that behavior is under review in [#16](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COHERO-RCT-analysis/issues/16). Scores are then derived from the item columns: `rowMeans(..., na.rm = TRUE)` averages available items within a row. It does not establish that an instrument permits a score with that many unanswered items; scoring rules remain to be verified against the instruments.

The baseline adherence and asthma-control groups are taken from each participant's baseline visit and set on all their visits, so a participant does not switch subgroup because a later score changes. For the R verbs in this block, see [Data transformation](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-transform.html) [@r4ds2].

```{r}
#| label: build-visit-data
#| eval: false
```

## Per protocol population

`clean_asthma_data_itt` retains the visit records for the intention-to-treat analysis, which compares participants by assigned arm. The project's per-protocol dataset is a filtered copy keeping observations on or before the app-glitch cutoff. Here, “per protocol” means this specific date restriction, not a general selection of participants who adhered to treatment. A missing visit date produces a missing comparison and is not retained by `filter(post_glitch_date == FALSE)`. The two datasets feed the same model code later.

```{r}
#| label: per-protocol-population
#| eval: false
```

## Study dates

Filtering to baseline makes a participant-level lookup table of consent and scheduled follow-up dates. The medication script joins this lookup onto app records to place them within each participant's follow-up. Check that the lookup has one row per participant: otherwise each medication record could match several rows. A blank follow-up date also needs attention because later comparisons against that date cannot establish whether a record is in the window.
